operationalization: Use repeated runs with measured and tightly controlled initial conditions, align trajectories, and quantify exact or local-pattern reproducibility as perturbation size is varied. Compare with runs receiving controlled environmental noise and with deliberately varied initial states.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public repeated-run experimental datasets for selected systems

candidate_datasets.name: Zenodo
candidate_datasets.role: public experimental datasets and simulation records

obstacles: Microscopic state cannot usually be reset exactly.
Unmeasured environmental inputs can mimic intrinsic sensitivity.
Deterministic chaos can make intrinsic dynamics nonrepeatable after tiny perturbations.
rationale: Controlled repeated-run datasets can test selected systems and compare mechanism predictions. Existing public data seldom measure perturbations finely enough, and repeatability is not uniquely diagnostic of intrinsic randomness generation.
